absolute_accessible.description: Is the simplified text easy to read and understand for a lay-person and do all (sub-)parts of the text make sense on their own (paragraphs, sentences)?
absolute_accessible.name: Absolute accessible

accessible_and_simple.description: Is the simplified text clearly easier to read and understandable to a non-expert, while still preserving the important meaning?
accessible_and_simple.name: Accessible and simple

actors_preserved.description: Are ALL responsible actors and affected parties correctly identified (no actors removed, generalized, or changed)?
actors_preserved.name: Actors preserved

actors_with_context.description: Are ALL responsible actors and affected parties correctly identified (no actors removed, generalized, or changed, allowing for the addition of actors from the context)?
actors_with_context.name: Actors with context

content_preserved.description: Does the simplified text preserve ALL important obligations, actions, and decisions from the original?
content_preserved.name: Content preserved

no_hallucination.description: Is the simplified text free of any new information, claims, or interpretations not present in the original?
no_hallucination.name: No hallucination

no_meaning_change.description: Does the simplified text avoid changing the meaning, strength, or conditions of the original (e.g. 'must' vs 'should', removing exceptions)?
no_meaning_change.name: No meaning change

obligations_complete.description: Does the simplified text contain EVERY obligation, recommendation, concern and decision from the original? Any important element that is omitted or compressed away fails.
obligations_complete.name: Obligations complete

actors_exact.description: Is it clear who is called on to act and who is affected, and does that match the record? Naming the country where the original text says 'the State party', or naming the body where it says 'the Committee', is CORRECT: the record supplies those and resolving them is the point. Fail only if an actor is dropped, swapped, invented, or generalized away (e.g. to 'the relevant authorities').
actors_exact.name: Actors exact

deontic_force.description: Is the strength of each ask preserved in BOTH directions? 'recommends'/'urges'/'calls upon' must not soften to 'should' or 'may', and 'should'/'consider' must not harden to 'must'. An imperative must not become an optional suggestion. Any shift either way fails.
deontic_force.name: Obligation strength

terms_of_art.description: Are legal and human-rights terms with defined meaning kept, or kept-and-glossed? Words like 'arbitrary', 'impunity', 'ratification', 'adequate housing', 'enforced disappearance', 'non-refoulement', 'reasonable accommodation' carry specific meaning that a plain synonym destroys. Replacing one with an everyday word fails ('arbitrary'->'unfair', 'impunity'->'lack of punishment'); keeping the term, with or without an added explanation, passes.
terms_of_art.name: Legal terms kept

references_precise.description: Are article citations, treaty and instrument names, general comment/recommendation numbers, named domestic laws, dates, statistics, case names and personal names all reproduced accurately? Dropping a citation such as '(arts. 12 and 24)' fails: it is the legal hook.
references_precise.name: References precise

scope_and_qualifiers.description: Do all conditions, exceptions, deadlines and scope markers survive with their force intact? 'including', 'in particular', 'such as' and 'especially' introduce non-exhaustive examples and must not be rewritten as complete lists; 'where appropriate' must not be dropped; explicit timeframes must remain.
scope_and_qualifiers.name: Scope & qualifiers

additions_explanatory_only.description: Is every piece of text not present in the original purely an explanation of a term that IS in the original (e.g. a parenthetical definition), and is each such explanation factually correct? Any new claim, interpretation, or inaccurate definition fails.
additions_explanatory_only.name: Additions explanatory only

plain_vocabulary.description: Judging the simplified text alone: is the vocabulary everyday language, with any remaining technical or legal term briefly explained on first use?
plain_vocabulary.name: Plain vocabulary

standalone_comprehension.description: Could a non-expert reading ONLY the simplified text correctly answer: who is being asked to do what, about which issue, in which country? If any of those is missing or guessable only from outside knowledge, fails.
standalone_comprehension.name: Stands alone
